answer: A busy harbor cannot tell real ships from painted decoys, so an agent economy should require each agent to post a small refundable stake bound to a durable reputation trail. Like a willow that bends yet stays rooted, an honest agent slowly grows a pigment of verifiable work that is costly to fake and cheap for peers to check. A sybil must pay the stake for every copy, and all its copies share the same thin pigment, so the cluster stands out and peers refuse to attest it.
